prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1097; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the northbound frontage road in Katy, Texas, when the rear of Driver 1's vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and was transported for evaluation. Officers observed rear-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle and a matching front-end impact on Driver 2's vehicle, and the damage appears consistent with the impact described by both drivers. Scene photographs confirm the positions of the vehicles and the general extent of the damage. No independent witnesses were located, and no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to the reporting officer. Driver 1 is listed as the named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle. Passenger, seated in the rear, stated the impact was brief but forceful. The exact seating position of Driver 1 at the moment of impact could not be fully established from statements and physical evidence, and it remains unclear whether the reported injury resulted from this collision. Follow-up medical records will be requested to clarify the connection.
